doc.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020

title: Count Basie's compliment in Newark
summary: Basie called him into his dressing room to praise his Louis-inspired playing.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: That is not — you mention Benny’s name in a crowd you know you get an hour’s worth, right? Now the other story is Count Basie. I did the warm-up act for Basie and I’m coming off stage and I’m walking past his dressing room, never met him, and I hear this voice, “Young man, young man, come in here.” I go in and there’s Count Basie. Now people don’t realize that in Newark that’s like walking in on Elvis or Michael Jackson, you know what I mean? He said, “I’ve been listening to you, you’ve been listening to Pops.” I said, “Yeah.” He said, “Well I just want to tell you something, you sound great, just keep on doing what you’ve been doing, don’t change anything.” I walked out of
there, oh my God. Count Basie takes time out of his life to call this white kid into his dressing room to validate his playing. Unbelievable. You know.
